Before you touch a contract, read this. I built this list from money I don't have anymore. Any single flag here is enough to walk away, no debate, no exception. This isn't paranoia, it's tuition I already paid, so you don't have to pay it too.

Contract Omens

  • Ownership still sitting with the dev, no verified multisig watching over it, that's a throne with one king and no council
  • Source code unverified on chain, that's a locked room and a bad feeling
  • Mint authority still alive, the supply isn't fixed, it's a promise that can be broken whenever they choose
  • Pause, blacklist, or blocklist function built into the bones of it, that's a leash, and you're not the one holding it
  • A sell tax that hides or shifts above 5 to 10%, that's a toll booth nobody warned you about

Liquidity Omens

  • Liquidity locked under 6 months, or locked behind a contract nobody's verified, that's a door that looks shut but isn't
  • LP tokens sitting in one wallet that could pull them any second, that's the rug, already threaded
  • Liquidity under 10% of market cap, the pool's too shallow to hold the weight of the hype

Holder Omens

  • Top 10 wallets holding 35% or more of supply, that's a room where a handful of hands can move the whole market on a whim
  • Top 10 wallets holding 50% or more, that's not a warning anymore, that's a certainty, treat it as manipulation and walk
  • Dev wallet holding 10% or more with no history of ever selling down, that's a story that hasn't been tested. Don't be the test

The Rule I Live By

One flag is a warning, and I still respect it. Two flags together, no matter the category, no matter how loud the timeline is screaming, is an automatic reject. Three cycles in, and that rule has never once failed me.

Purpose

The Saga does not end. Three cycles deep and still rising, I've walked through fire and come out heavier in gold than I went in. This is not a hobby, it's a discipline, and discipline compounds like nothing else in this game. These are the Commandments, ten of them, covering every asset I trade under this name. They exist to protect what I've built before they ever try to grow it further. None are optional. None bend for conviction, urgency, or a market that's screaming at you to break them anyway.

Commandment 1: Position Sizing

Market Cap TierClassificationMax Allocation
Under $1MHigh risk5% of portfolio
$1M to $10MMedium risk10% of portfolio
High conviction, any tierRequires thesis15% of portfolio

How much of yourself you put into one bet. Fifteen percent is the ceiling, and it's earned, not assumed, conviction that size needs a documented thesis with at least 3 independent catalysts written down before you buy, never invented after. Nothing crosses 15%. Not once, not for anyone.

Commandment 2: Entry Criteria

  • Pooled liquidity: minimum $50,000
  • Liquidity to market cap ratio: minimum 10%
  • 24 hour volume sufficient to support the position without the trade itself moving the market
  • Price impact: single buy does not exceed 2% of pool liquidity
  • Exit feasibility: full position could be liquidated within roughly 2% of current price

Before I enter, the trade has to earn it. Miss one of these and I pass, every single time, no matter how good the chart looks.

Commandment 3: Contract and Liquidity Diligence

  • Ownership not renounced, and no verified multisig
  • Source code unverified on chain
  • Active mint authority
  • Pause, blacklist, or blocklist function present
  • Hidden or dynamic sell tax above 5 to 10%
  • Liquidity locked under 6 months, or unverified locker
  • LP tokens concentrated in a single withdrawable wallet

The chain doesn't lie, but it hides things if you don't look closely. Any one of these is sufficient to reject the trade, and I don't look back once I do.

Commandment 4: Holder Concentration

  • Reject if top 10 wallets hold more than 35% of supply, excluding LP and burn addresses
  • 50% or more among the top 10 is treated as a manipulation signal, not a gray area

Power concentrated in a few hands is power that can crush you the moment it moves.

Commandment 5: Stop Loss Policy

Market Cap TierStop Loss
Under $1MNegative 50% from entry
$1M or moreNegative 25% from entry

Every position gets a floor before it gets a dollar. Stops are set at entry, may be tightened to protect what I've won, and are never loosened to protect my ego. The stop is sacred. It doesn't move for hope.

Commandment 6: Take Profit Structure

  • 25% of position sold at 2x
  • 25% of position sold at 5x
  • 25% of position sold at 10x
  • Remaining 25% held as a runner with a trailing stop

Winning is a discipline too, maybe the harder one. Some positions are meant to become legend, and you don't know which ones until you let the last quarter run.

Commandment 7: Portfolio Limits

  • Maximum 10 concurrent open positions
  • Maximum 25% of total trading capital newly deployed within any 24 hour period

Even conviction has a ceiling. Spread too thin and you're not trading anymore, you're gambling with extra steps.

Commandment 8: Daily Loss Limit

  • Trading halts for the day upon a cumulative 25% portfolio drawdown within 24 hours
  • Two consecutive days of hitting this limit triggers a mandatory 48 hour suspension and a full review before resuming

Bad days happen to everyone who's stayed in this long enough to call it a career. Capital doesn't get to bleed out just because I'm stubborn.

Commandment 9: Trade Log Requirements

  • Entry price, market cap, and liquidity at entry
  • Position size as % of portfolio
  • Thesis and catalysts
  • Exit price and final P&L, recorded within 1 hour of exit

What isn't written down gets repeated. I read the log back every week, hunting for what cost me: sizing up after a win because I felt invincible, revenge trading after a loss because I felt owed, skipping diligence because FOMO was louder than discipline. The log doesn't lie, even when I want it to.

Commandment 10: Touch Grass

  • Drink water and stand up, stretch, every hour
  • Take a real break away from the charts every 4 hours, not a scroll break, an actual break
  • Eat a healthy meal away from the charts, not hunched over a candle
  • No trading after 12 or more consecutive hours of screen time without a real break away from the charts
  • Decisions made while sleep deprived, emotionally flooded, intoxicated, or trading out of boredom are void, regardless of how good the setup looks
  • One full day per week with no charts, no positions checked, no exceptions
  • Meditate, walk, exercise, hike, bike, whatever it is, just go touch some actual grass
  • Winning streaks and losing streaks both distort judgment. Step outside before sizing up after either one
  • If trading has started to feel like the only thing going on in your life, that is the signal to stop and reset, not to push through

Capital survives bad markets. It rarely survives a trader who never touches grass. Rise, but rise rested.

This is binding on everything I trade under the Saga name, and it stays binding until I sit down and rewrite it myself, with a clear head, not a hot one.

What This Tool Does

7 FIGURE SAGA is the workflow I built for myself, three cycles in, because guessing was expensive and memory is unreliable. Research the asset, size the position, track it while it breathes, close it when it's time, and look back at the whole story later. Every tab feeds the next, so walk them in order and the tool does the remembering for you.

Not Financial Advice

This tool tracks and organizes what I do, it isn't telling you what to do. The scoring, the flags, the Commandments, that's one trader's discipline, not a guarantee, and not professional financial advice. Meme coins especially are high risk, most go to zero, that's just the truth of this game. Nothing here, not the prices, not the market caps, not the scores pulled from DexScreener, CoinGecko, or Finnhub, is promised to be accurate in the moment you're looking at it. Do your own research. Never risk what you can't survive losing. My thoughts, your decisions.

Portfolio

Home base. Total value up top, a pie of where your capital's sitting, a bar chart of cost basis against what it's worth now, and every holding laid out plain. Hit Refresh prices to pull the latest on anything with a chart link attached.

Open

Where positions are born, grow, and get trimmed. A buy on a ticker you already hold adds to it, a sell reduces it and fully closes the position once the quantity hits zero. Recent activity at the bottom keeps the log, edit or delete any entry and everything above it recalculates itself automatically.

Closed

The full record of everything I've walked away from, dates opened and closed, cost basis, exit value, and final PNL in both percent and dollars. This is where the real lessons live, if you're willing to read them honestly.

Research

Run anything through the Setup Quality Score before you commit capital to it. Liquidity, volume, holders, website, socials, dev wallet, holder concentration, feed it in and get a score out of 100 and a suggested position size. Mark "Did you buy this token?" as Y and fill in tokens bought and cost basis, and logging the score opens the position for you automatically.

Watchlist

Assets I'm watching but haven't touched yet, split into memes, crypto, and stocks. Comes stocked with a starter list in each. Add anything with a chart link, then refresh individually or all at once, none of it counts against your portfolio until you actually buy in. Every field stays editable if something needs correcting.

Commandments

The full law I trade by. Position sizing, entry criteria, stops, targets, and the tenth Commandment that matters more than people think, stepping away from the screen. Read it once, then read it again after your first real loss, it hits different.

Omens

The fast scan before you buy. Contract, liquidity, and holder omens, distilled to what actually matters. One omen is a warning I still respect. Two together is a reject, no matter how good the story sounds.

How to load any asset

Every "Chart link" field in this app works the same way: paste one link, everything else fills in. You never need to type a link format from memory, just copy the address bar from one of these three sites:

  • Meme coins and most crypto tokens: dexscreener.com, search the ticker, copy the pair page URL
  • Major coins (BTC, ETH, SOL, and similar): coingecko.com, search the coin, copy the page URL
  • Stocks and ETFs: google.com/finance, search the ticker, copy the page URL

Paste that link into Research, when opening a new position, or when adding something to Watchlist, and the ticker's contract address, website, and X page fill in on their own when that data is available. Nothing is locked, if it grabs something wrong or misses a field, every field stays editable by hand.

Stocks need one extra step: add your own free Finnhub API key in the Profile card up top, that's what actually fetches stock prices. Crypto and meme coins work with no key needed.

Chart links and live prices

That same link also powers the Refresh price buttons across Portfolio, Open, and Watchlist. DexScreener carries liquidity too, CoinGecko and stocks don't track that number, it's a DEX-pool-specific thing. If a refresh ever fails, the tool tells you rather than showing you a stale number that lies to your face, just update the value by hand as a fallback.

Your data

Everything you enter stays yours, private to your own account, nobody else using this tool can see it. Use Save Your File any time to back it up, and Open Your Saved File to bring it back, even into a newer version of this tool if one comes your way later.
